newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils close steady after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils close steady after U.S. data.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices closed steady on Friday following the release of the USDA's supply and demand report.
The USDA cut U.S. soybeans stocks by 15 million bushels from it's last estimate to 125 million bushels the lowest stocks for 20 years.
European traders expected Chicago futures to soar and there was a scramble for material prior to the Chicago opening.

However, after early gains the U.S. market turned lower as players took note of the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush report which showed a 25.94 million bushel soybean crush, one million bushels below trade expectations.
"People who bought at the top this afternoon are feeling pretty sick right now," said one trader.
In the palm oil market players were mostly sidelined ahead of the official data from the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) which is due for release on Tuesday.
Crude palm oil closed $2.50 to $5 up after Apr traded at $560, May/Jul at $577.50 and $560 and Jul/Sep at $555 a tonne cif.
Products closed with RBD palm oil and palm olein $2.50 to $5 higher with no further business reported during the afternoon.
Coconut oil was mixed with sellers $2.50 up to $2.50 down after Apr/May $720 and Jun/Jul $710 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil finished unchanged to $2.50 up.
In the soft oils sector soy oil was quoted 1.75 guilders up after 105 guilders was paid for Aug/Oct.
Dutch/EU rape oil was also 1.75 guilders higher after May/Jul traded from 104.25 up to 105.50 guilders and Aug/Oct from 102.00 upto 03.75 in 0.25 guilder steps.
